key_insight: In this sepsis study—not cancer drug discovery—three of five language models exceeded physicians’ diagnostic accuracy after biomarker disclosure.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest potential for biomarker-informed diagnostic support, but do not establish safety or effectiveness in clinical practice.
method: Evaluated five locally deployed language models on six anonymised clinical cases with Sepsis-3 reference diagnoses.
Compared model responses with those of 353 clinicians before and after biomarker disclosure.
Assessed demographic and language sensitivity, reproducibility, and confidence calibration.
evidence_signal: After biomarker disclosure, accuracy was 91% for Qwen3.8-27B, 86% for its quantised variant, and 83% for Gemma-4-31B, versus 61% for physicians.
watch_item: Only six cases were evaluated in silico; language-related bias and difficulty with post-surgical sepsis warrant broader validation.
paper_title: Can Language Models Diagnose Sepsis? A Head-to-Head Evaluation Against 353 Physicians
